chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Alawi, from Sahl ibn Jamhur, from Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn al-Uranni, from Amr ibn Jumi' who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the mosques with pictures, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that, but it will not harm you today, and if the justice had been established, you would see what would be done regarding that.'

key_terms.الْعَدْلُ: The Justice (referring to the rise of Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in mosques that contain images or pictures?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules that praying in mosques adorned with images is disliked (makruh) but does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the practical leniency of the current era. He foresees a stricter enforcement in the time of the Qaim (the Mahdi), when divine justice is fully established, indicating that the prohibition is tied to the context of idolatrous practices that will be eradicated. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the severity of the ruling escalates with the purification of religious practice under the Mahdi's leadership.
